sources.entry: DisplayMenu - Simple (bare-bones) macOS menubar extra to apply display presets.

summary.one_liner: A bare-bones macOS menubar extra that applies saved display presets (screen resolutions, mirroring, and dock settings) from a JSON config file.
summary.what_it_does: The app shows a menu in the macOS menubar from which you can apply display presets. A preset can cover screen resolutions, mirroring configuration, and dock settings. There is no configuration GUI: presets are defined in a JSON file placed at ~/Library/Application Support/com.chriswarrick.DisplayMenu/DisplayMenu.json, and a sample file is included with the distribution. Screen IDs for each display are obtained with a command-line PrintScreenIDs executable, or by compiling the included Swift source. The README's roadmap lists planned work to change only differing settings, show the current preset in the menu, and build a configuration GUI.
use_cases: switch display resolution with one click
toggle display mirroring presets on macOS
save and restore dock and screen layouts
quick display setup for docked laptop
how_to_run: Download the app from the link in the README (Download section).
Run ./PrintScreenIDs from the command line to find the ScreenIDs for your displays, or compile the .swift source file yourself.
Create the JSON configuration file at ~/Library/Application Support/com.chriswarrick.DisplayMenu/DisplayMenu.json, starting from the sample file included with the distribution.
Put your resolution, mirroring, and dock settings for each preset into the JSON file, using the ScreenIDs found earlier.
Launch DisplayMenu and choose a preset from the menubar menu.
notable: Presets bundle screen resolution, mirroring, and dock settings into one menu choice
Configured entirely through a hand-written JSON file; no configuration GUI yet
Includes a PrintScreenIDs command-line tool to look up display IDs
caveats: No configuration GUI; setup requires writing a JSON file by hand
Requires finding ScreenIDs with a command-line tool or compiling Swift source
Roadmap items (changing only differing settings, showing current preset) are not yet implemented
